title: Stock market today: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq enters correction in AI trade meltdown
summary:
US stocks plunged on Thursday as AI and chip stocks sold off, erasing the gains from Wednesday's post-election rally.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) tumbled 3.4%, or more than 1,800 points.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 4.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) dropped 5.5%, with the tech-heavy index closing in correction territory.
Wall Street unloaded this year's AI winners, while large-cap tech stocks saw the worst day since the COVID-19 pandemic sell-off.
Oil prices rose amid uncertainty that President Trump would pursue a deal with Iran to end the war in the Middle East.

title: Claude AI can plug directly into your bank account
summary:

title: Bluetooth 7 Speeds Are Set to Quadruple in 2027, Especially for Audio
summary:
On Thursday, the Bluetooth Special Interest Group, the trade association that oversees Bluetooth, officially unveiled Bluetooth High Data Throughput, a flagship upgrade set to arrive as part of the Bluetooth Core 7.0 standard.
Bluetooth is still the most popular medium-to-short-range wireless standard for connecting devices.
The biggest change in this update is a new physical layer for Bluetooth.
Improvements in the physical layer can have very significant effects on all Bluetooth communications.
In this case, new modulation schemes let the physical layer handle data more efficiently and transmit more data at once, which is why the speed increases are so significant.

title: OpenAI lays out new policy framework for data centers
summary:
OpenAI has backed a new set of measures the company says will give communities a greater say in data center development, according to a policy announcement shared with POLITICO.
The framework shows how one of the world's leading artificial intelligence labs is attempting to reconcile public opposition to the infrastructure with Silicon Valley's need to keep building data centers to support artificial intelligence development.
It would also allow providers to throttle power to data centers during periods of high demand.
OpenAI also unveiled new commitments to communities near its data centers, including a promise to pay for the full cost of energy usage and infrastructure, prioritize closed-loop cooling systems that use less water and work with local unions to fill jobs at the data centers.
They also announced plans to rebrand data centers as "compute campuses," an apparent acknowledgement of the widespread public dislike for the infrastructure's longtime name.
